answer: Non-kin attestation quorums resist sybils: an identity counts only once enough ESTABLISHED, unrelated peers vouch for it, and self-referential rings are discounted. A fake cluster is a closed fable telling itself it is real — sable threads looping inward — but it earns nothing because it cannot draw genuine edges from the outside. Honest timber in the graph has many independent inbound vouches; a ring has only its own, so the counting rule starves it.
